To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) a temporal logic with constrained events can be used for specifying test purposes for testing concurrency; and 2) the logic can be used to derive symbolic test cases for concurrent programs.

1) a new logic is proposed to represent data dependency constraints in test purposes, 2) a new symbolic test generation algorithm is proposed that can generate test cases with verdict conditions that incorporate the data dependency constraints, and 3) the new logic and test generation algorithm are demonstrated to be useful by a case study on testing a cache coherence protocol.

1) the temporal logic of constrained events, TLCE, can express not only event order constraints, but also data dependency constraints between event parameters, and can be used to specify test purposes; 2) a TLCE-based test case generation algorithm can be used to generate symbolic test cases that include the given data dependency constraints in the form of verdict conditions; 3) the approach is effective in deriving symbolic test cases from a given TLCE specification.

the development of a test generation method for concurrent programs.

the development of a symbolic test generation approach based on a temporal logic with constrained events, which is able to automatically derive test cases from a formal description of a concurrent system.
